source: "Seed Production" (ដំណាំកម្មពូជ) training deck, Provincial Department of Agriculture Kampong Thom (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកំពង់ធំ), compiled/presented by Tem Seng (temseng@yahoo.com). Explanatory Khmer narration is set in the legacy (non-Unicode) Limon font and could not be extracted; this entry draws on the deck's clean English-language slides (pp. 8-13) plus a Khmer worked-example slide whose numerals and formula structure (but not the surrounding Khmer sentences) were legible. No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL visible in the document.
text:
Before multiplying seed (growing one seed class up into a larger quantity of the next class down the certification chain), the source lists several factors a seed grower or seed-multiplication officer should plan around:

Climatic factors: light, temperature, rainfall, wind, soil, and season all affect how well a seed-multiplication plot performs and should be matched to the variety being multiplied.

Agronomic factors: fertilizer program, irrigation, weed control, and disease/pest control all need to be planned for specifically, since a seed-multiplication plot is held to a higher purity and quality standard than an ordinary grain plot.

Previous cropping / rotation interval: volunteer plants from a different variety or species grown in the same field previously can contaminate the new seed crop. The source recommends leaving enough interval between two seed crops in the same field (allowing for seed dormancy to pass) that any previous crop's shed seed has already germinated and been cleared out, rather than lying dormant in the soil ready to come up as a contaminant inside the new seed crop.

Planning checklist: which class of certified seed is required, land selection, how much seed is needed, and a time table / crop schedule.

The source also gives a 'multiplication factor' calculation for estimating how much seed of one class is needed to produce a target quantity of the next class: multiplication factor = yield harvested per unit area (from the seed sown) divided by the seed rate that was sown on that same unit area. Worked example given in the source: if a grower wants to produce 20,000 kg of Registered seed, and the seeding rate for Foundation seed is 40 kg/rai with an expected yield of 800 kg/rai of Registered seed from that planting, the multiplication factor is 800 divided by 40 = 20. To reach the 20,000 kg target, the grower would then need 20,000 divided by 20 = 1,000 kg of Foundation seed in stock to plant. (Note: 'rai' is a Thai land-area unit, about 1,600 square meters or roughly 0.16 hectares, used in this source's original worked example; convert to hectares before applying the method to a Cambodian field.)
